source.title: Toward Secure Tuning: Mitigating Security Risks from Instruction Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Yan-Rui Du; Feng-Lei Fan; Sen-Dong Zhao; Jia-Wei Cao; Ming Ma; Dan-Yang Zhao; Shu-Ren Qi; Ting Liu; Bing Qin

record.tranche_reason: The study applies standard instruction fine-tuning with benign or harmful training data to chat models and measures security outcomes including attack success rate, comparable to the original fine-tuning claim. It is not an explicit replication and uses different data and training details.
record.gate_note: The standard-IFT results report averages across six red-team and jailbreak test sets; those aggregate results are recorded below. The paper also reports classifier-based security-feature-space analysis and module perturbations, but those are not refusal or harmful-compliance measurements. The SWAT method-comparison results are not recorded as rows for the original fine-tuning effect.
record.test_reason: Mainly a defense-method (SWAT) paper, but it reports security of base vs standard-IFT models for benign and attack-mixed fine-tuning. It uses Qi et al.'s GPT-Judge harmfulness score plus keyword ASR, so its own results bear on V1 and V2. Differences from the original: LoRA, 10 epochs, task data plus Alpaca.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that security feature-space drift is one reason IFT introduces security risks. They report that SWAT, which warms up robust modules first, mitigates risk with little task-performance loss, and that residual risks show drift is not the only cause.
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard LoRA IFT with task datasets and 10,000 Alpaca dialogue samples; the attack setting adds 100 affirmative attack samples to the task mix. It is not an explicit replication of the original study's exact data and training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The benign-IFT result varies by model and task dataset; Llama2 7B is evaluated with both UltraInteract and GSM8K, while Llama3 8B and Qwen2 7B are reported with UltraInteract. Security evaluation averages six attack sets, which can differ in their individual outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: For Llama2 7B, a probe classifier trained on one model's last-token representation loses accuracy on the other's: C_base 99.00%→80.50%, C_tuned 100.00%→77.00%. Similar drops appear for Llama3 8B and Qwen2 7B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction fine-tuning causes drift in the representation space separating benign from malicious instructions.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning only the first 4 layers yields higher harmfulness (HS ~2.55–3.79) than fine-tuning only the last 4 layers (HS ~1.39–1.54), across the three models (Fig. 6–8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning updates to early layers erode safety more than updates to deep layers.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), 2024
record.problems: The reported security metrics are averages across attack sets; no error bars or confidence intervals are stated. The attack-IFT result is reported for Llama2 7B only and is not near-complete compliance. The classifier analysis measures classification accuracy rather than harmful-response behavior.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6 also list individual attack-set cells and comparisons with SWAT and other defense methods. The rows here retain the explicit AVG results for standard IFT; individual cells were not assigned because the supplied table text is flattened and the mapping is not reliably recoverable throughout.

untested.parts: Only 100 harmful examples, mixed into ~16.7k benign samples, on Llama2 7B. Untested: the few-to-few-hundred range, harmful-only fine-tuning, and other models.
Only ordinary task data (UltraInteract, GSM8K) plus Alpaca. Untested: carefully selected benign data, and data-size or epoch variation.
Not tested; no per-token KL or position analysis.
Not tested as a bypass of the aligned model. CompObj/PAIR prompt-level 'start with' attacks are used only as evaluation sets after fine-tuning. No prefilling or decoding manipulation.
Module perturbation is measured by probe-classifier accuracy, not refusal behaviour. The layer-restricted fine-tuning HS result concerns where updates erode safety, not where safety resides.
Not tested; SWAT is a warm-up method, not a deepening of alignment beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Direct harmful-request cells for standard IFT vs BASE, which isolate harmful compliance from jailbreak sets. Llama2 UltraInteract: Advbench 30.91%, CatQA 36.36% (base 1.82%/0.00%). Llama2 GSM8K: 24.55%/20.91%. Llama2 Attack IFT: 60.00%/58.18%. Llama3: 40.91%/50.00% (base 3.64%/10.91%). Qwen2: 38.18%/59.09% (base 2.73%/9.09%).
missing.locator: Tables 2, 3, 5, 6, Advbench and CatQA columns, IFT row

missing.what: Layer-restricted fine-tuning harmfulness (first 4 vs last 4 layers). The flattened figure text makes the per-model HS mapping ambiguous.

record.verdict_notes: Training is heavy (10 epochs, lr 2e-4), which may inflate erosion relative to the originals. ASR is keyword-based; HS uses GPT-4o GPT-Judge. No uncertainty is reported. The V1 verdict is limited because the design never compares attack IFT against harmful-only or no-benign training. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests 100 affirmative attack examples mixed into task-training data on Llama2 7B. It does not test a range from a few to a few hundred examples, or whether refusal is removed almost entirely across models.
The benign-data tests use task data plus Alpaca dialogue data; they do not test a broad range of ordinary or carefully selected benign datasets or data sizes.
Per-token KL divergence and its distribution across response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, suffix attacks, and decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior. Module robustness is assessed through classifier performance, not causal changes in harmful-compliance behavior.
Whether data or the training objective causes first-token shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond initial tokens and its robustness.
